nodes.label: Archived Reflection Context
nodes.rationale: Immutability of the archived record is what makes it safe for Knowledge, Habit and Goal engines to consume at next boot without reading a reflection still being generated.

nodes.label: Reflection Confidence
nodes.rationale: Certainty metric over the strength of supporting evidence; low-confidence reflections are hidden rather than shown, prioritizing accuracy over speculation.

nodes.label: Reflection Context
nodes.rationale: Single conceptual output carrying progress, growth, patterns, achievements, challenges, supporting evidence, confidence and time period, so downstream engines read one compact model instead of parsing raw tables.

nodes.label: Reflection Engine
nodes.rationale: Retrospective progress synthesis is kept out of the active dialogue path so growth analysis never interrupts conversation; it synthesizes trends from facts Memory already stores rather than creating new facts.

nodes.label: AI Context Engine (prompt compiler)
nodes.rationale: Kept strictly downstream of resolution so prompt formatting and provider communication never absorb context reconciliation logic.

nodes.label: Context Relevance Filter
nodes.rationale: Relevance over quantity: discard low-relevance or redundant detail so prompts stay focused and small.

nodes.label: Context Resolution Engine (CRE)
nodes.rationale: A dedicated orchestrator prevents each engine from needing knowledge of the others' states. Without central coordination the context package becomes cluttered, contradictory and unfocused. The CRE resolves context but never creates it, and is prohibited from querying subsystem internals or database tables directly.

nodes.label: Resolved Context
nodes.rationale: One immutable, prioritized model of the user's situation, so any downstream consumer (prompt formatter, notification dispatcher, initiative evaluator) reads the same structure.

nodes.label: Conversation Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Receives Initiative Decisions and executes dialogue actions; it decides how to communicate while the Initiative Engine decides if communication is appropriate.

nodes.label: Initiative Decision
nodes.rationale: Captures outcome (Silence, Suggestion, Question, Reminder), confidence, supporting evidence, user benefit, timing suitability and why silence was overridden — making every intervention auditable.

nodes.label: Initiative Engine
nodes.rationale: Separating initiative from response generation means proactivity is judged objectively before any text is written. Consumes only the Resolved Context; consuming individual subsystem outputs directly is prohibited.

nodes.label: Adaptive Memory Engine
nodes.rationale: Persistent storage layer that must never communicate directly with AI models; standardizing on local primitive schemas lets data be encrypted or managed locally before any reasoning client touches it.

nodes.label: AI Context Engine (API/prompt translator)
nodes.rationale: Sole place where provider-specific prompt structure exists, so switching between local ONNX models and cloud APIs touches only this layer.

nodes.label: Context Builder (understanding assembler)
nodes.rationale: Required intermediate stage that formats logical data before any API payload is built.

nodes.label: Reasoning Model (stateless inference core)
nodes.rationale: Statelessness is deliberate: reasoning holds no memory, so all durable state stays in the local database.

nodes.label: Recall Engine
nodes.rationale: Relevance selector; together with the Memory Engine it is solely responsible for selecting and delivering primitive candidate models.

nodes.label: Story (narrative grouping anchor)
nodes.rationale: Humans organize experience as narratives, not timelines. Stories are poly-hierarchical so one memory node can belong to several journeys at once, and recalling one memory raises retrieval probability of related milestones in the same arc. Memories in completed stories are preserved as high-importance experiential context instead of decaying out.

nodes.label: Identity Layer
nodes.rationale: Never manually configured; traits, work styles, values and strengths emerge from long-term patterns across Events, Memories, Stories and physical behavior, and may strengthen, weaken or evolve as focus changes.

nodes.label: Context Package
nodes.rationale: Logical structured data rather than an LLM-specific prompt, so downstream adapters can translate the same package for Gemini, OpenAI or local offline models. Supports multiple situational types (Working, Reflection, Planning). Status: Accepted.

nodes.label: Goal Context
nodes.rationale: The single interface other systems use, so downstream engines never query project or memory tables to find goals.

nodes.label: Knowledge Context
nodes.rationale: Structured competency model that keeps explanations matched to the user's level and stays compact as memory grows; preserves originating subsystem, supporting evidence and confidence rating (Provenance Preservation).

nodes.label: Relationship Context
nodes.rationale: Isolating social data in one structured output also serves privacy: records can be inspected or cleared without touching the rest of the database.

nodes.label: Habit Context
nodes.rationale: Neutral, evidence-linked pattern model (e.g. a late-evening focus routine verified against recorded work sessions); preserves originating subsystem, supporting evidence and confidence rating. Events represent history while the Habit engine models abstract frequency and probability distributions.

nodes.label: Workspace Canvas Shell (Shell.tsx)
nodes.rationale: Per-page navigation layouts duplicate layout code and cause layout shift during transitions. A global parent shell in src/app/shell/ owns sidebar, top bar, background glows, responsive behavior and command palettes; routes mount as nested children in its <main>. Rejected putting the layout in TanStack Router's __root.tsx because full-screen boot animations and error boundaries must bypass the sidebar. Trade-off: pages must fit the shell's grid. Status: Accepted.

nodes.label: Dynamic Tool Registry (toolsRegistry)
nodes.rationale: Hardcoding links in Sidebar.tsx scatters feature flags and visibility rules across layout files. A centralized registry in src/akira-os/tools/registry.ts holds paths, categories, ready states and visibility restrictions; the sidebar queries it. Rejected scanning the TanStack route tree because route paths carry no category or developer-mode flag. Cost: new modules must be registered in both the route tree and the registry. Status: Accepted.

nodes.label: ADR-001: Separation of Memory and AI Models
nodes.norm_label: adr-001: separation of memory and ai models
nodes.rationale: Coupling memory storage to a specific LLM API limits portability, compromises local-first privacy, and exposes the system to provider lock-in and breaking changes. A unidirectional pipeline keeps the persistent schema unaffected by provider switches or inference failures. Status: Accepted.

nodes.label: ADR-002: Story-First Memory Architecture
nodes.rationale: Flat chronological logs and raw-chunk vector similarity leave the companion blind to the larger journeys a user is navigating, producing fragmented feedback. Status: Accepted.

nodes.label: ADR-003: Emergent Identity Discovery
nodes.rationale: Static configuration forms capture self-declared aspirations rather than observed behavior and require ongoing manual curation. Status: Accepted.

nodes.label: ADR-005: Companion Core Behavioral Model
nodes.rationale: Engagement-maximizing chatbots prioritize superficial validation and screen time, which is counter-productive to growth and fosters dependence. Status: Accepted.

nodes.label: ADR-006: Deterministic Presence Subsystem
nodes.rationale: Presence (session mode, return state, elapsed gaps, continuity) is computed by local deterministic rules instead of runtime cognitive inference: deterministic logic runs in under a millisecond, incurs no token cost, and yields reproducible thresholds where a probabilistic model would be inconsistent. Threshold changes move to local configuration rather than prompt edits. Status: Proposed.

nodes.label: ADR-007: Ephemeral Session-Scoped Companion State Layer
nodes.norm_label: adr-007: ephemeral session-scoped companion state layer
nodes.rationale: Rejected writing every focus shift to GENESIS (write amplification, database bloat, slower semantic recall) and rejected stateless per-turn prompting (contextually blind between turns, forces massive event logs into reasoning engines). Status: Proposed.

nodes.label: ADR-008: Dedicated Goal Subsystem
nodes.rationale: Rejected embedding goals in Memory (historical and immutable vs. future-oriented and hierarchical), in Identity (traits evolve slowly, goals change often), and in Projects (goals cross project boundaries or exist with no workspace at all). Division of time: Memory stores the past, State the present, Goals the future path, Identity the character. Status: Proposed.

nodes.label: ADR-009: Dedicated Knowledge Subsystem
nodes.rationale: Rejected ad-hoc reconstruction of skill dependencies from flat memory logs (severe latency as logs grow) and in-prompt competency inference (inconsistent behavior — alternating between explaining basics and assuming mastery — plus prompt inflation). Status: Proposed.

nodes.label: ADR-010: Dedicated Relationship Subsystem
nodes.rationale: Rejected raw semantic tags in Memory (parsing thousands of events per turn to extract active contacts and open plans is slow) and modeling contacts as identity traits (identity evolves slowly, contacts and collaborative goals change frequently — blending them violates single responsibility). Memory stores events, Identity models the user's character, Relationship models the external social network. Status: Proposed.

nodes.label: ADR-011: Evidence-Based Habit Subsystem
nodes.rationale: Rejected gamified streaks and scoreboards (a broken streak from a real-world interruption demotivates, prioritizing app engagement over growth) and proactive alert schedulers (intrusive, disrupts deep focus, behaves like a micro-managing boss). The engine observes routines but never enforces them, adapting when the user's schedule changes rather than shaming a broken streak. Status: Proposed.

nodes.label: ADR-012: Dedicated Retrospective Reflection Subsystem
nodes.rationale: Rejected in-conversation reflection (heavy cross-database queries mid-sentence stall the chat) and memory-triggered reflection (recomputing trend lines, skill dependencies and habit stability on every minor write wastes cycles and slows writes). Chosen: asynchronous execution after sessions close, giving zero conversation latency and cached, consistent summaries. Status: Proposed.

nodes.label: ADR-013: Dedicated Context Resolution Subsystem
nodes.rationale: Rejected distributed self-prioritization (engines blind to each other produce bloated, conflicting context updates) and embedding resolution in the AI Context Engine (blends resolution into prompt code, hard to audit or test, and locks out non-LLM consumers such as local automation). Status: Proposed.

nodes.label: ADR-014: Dedicated Initiative Subsystem and Silence-by-Default Design
nodes.norm_label: adr-014: dedicated initiative subsystem and silence-by-default design
nodes.rationale: Rejected per-engine self-initiated alerts (simultaneous interventions cause prompt fatigue) and LLM-decided proactivity (conversational models are trained to keep users talking, making silence impossible to guarantee or explain, and inflating token cost). A deterministic engine defaulting to No Action makes every intervention traceable. Status: Proposed.

nodes.label: AKIRA ADR Process
nodes.rationale: Specifications describe what was built and how; ADRs preserve the contextual trade-offs and debates so future contributors and AI agents understand why. Standard sections: Status, Context, Decision, Reasoning, Consequences. ADRs record why, not how — no schemas, API specs, coding patterns or UI designs.

nodes.label: GENESIS Engine Roadmap
nodes.rationale: Core cognitive milestones: enhance long-term story consolidation, build proactive initiative trigger evaluations, extend AI context-resolution performance.

nodes.label: Preserve Uncertainty
nodes.rationale: Prefer producing no reflection at all over a speculative or misleading summary; uncertainty is propagated rather than rounded away.

nodes.label: Temporal Decoupling of Reflection
nodes.rationale: Reflection consumes finalized active contexts at session end and downstream engines may only read previously archived reflections at their next initialization. This prevents circular dependencies between Reflection and the engines that feed it.

nodes.label: Resolve Conflict without Discarding
nodes.rationale: Contradictions between subsystems are included with a note on the conflict rather than thrown out; the state engine (present behavior) acts as tie-breaker and overall confidence is lowered.

nodes.label: Provenance Preservation
nodes.rationale: Prioritizing and reconciling must never strip originating metadata (originating subsystem, supporting evidence, confidence rating). Every resolved understanding stays traceable and auditable back to the subsystem that produced it.

nodes.label: Silence is the Default
nodes.rationale: Engagement-maximizing notification loops create fatigue and erode trust, so no action is the default state; weak evidence, low confidence, ambiguity, conflicting priorities or deep-focus timing all fall back to silence.

nodes.label: User Autonomy Protection
nodes.rationale: The companion never insists, demands, coerces or overrides user choices, and never creates artificial urgency through alerts or countdowns.

nodes.label: Traceable Lineage (Provenance)
nodes.rationale: Because identity is inferred rather than declared, every trait must carry a confidence rating and explicit references to the supporting memories, so it can be inspected or corrected — this is what makes an inferred profile trustworthy.

nodes.label: Selective Context / Selective Omission
nodes.rationale: Feeding raw databases into reasoning models causes low-quality responses and high query cost, so the builder enforces dynamic constraints and prunes irrelevant context (e.g. omitting completed chores during coding tasks) to prevent cognitive noise. Assembly happens on-device, keeping the system offline-ready.

nodes.label: Trustworthy Growth Companion
nodes.rationale: Balances Truth, Compassion, Accountability and Humility; chooses truth over comfort because empty reassurance does not clear bottlenecks, acknowledges incomplete evidence to avoid false confidence, and accepts user overrides instantly without friction. Excludes sycophantic praise, manufactured optimism, emotional manipulation and guilt-trips.

nodes.label: Offline-First Resilience
nodes.rationale: A core system principle: presence calculations must stay fully active in isolated environments with zero connectivity, which rules out any external intelligence call on the hot path.

nodes.label: Ephemeral Session-Scoped State
nodes.rationale: Memory stores what the user has achieved; State tracks what they are doing right now. The layer initializes at session start, evolves in memory, and expires at session end — only a consolidated summary is committed via Reflection. Everything in it is volatile and lost on termination unless summarized.

nodes.label: Evidence Verification (user correction as evidence)
nodes.rationale: An explicit user correction of an inferred level is treated as verified evidence and prioritized in future reasoning, while previous inferences are kept so the change stays explainable rather than silently overwritten.

nodes.label: Consistent Temporal Reference
nodes.rationale: Retrospective intervals are evaluated against a reference supplied by the Companion Platform rather than local device clocks, preventing synchronization drift across devices and preserving chronological sequencing during multi-device use.

nodes.label: Immutable ADR History
nodes.rationale: An accepted ADR is never edited to change a historical decision; a reversal gets a new ADR that supersedes it, with the original marked Superceded and linked. Specifications evolve toward a current target state, ADRs stay a chronological log — keeping the two separate preserves full traceability.

nodes.rationale: Security is treated as a fundamental design principle shaping every architectural layer, not a post-implementation feature, because the data AKIRA collects is deeply intimate.

nodes.label: Desktop-First Architecture

nodes.label: Active and Idle Protection
nodes.rationale: At rest, files and logs use native encryption; in use, temporary context packages, in-memory caches and chat contexts must be scrubbed when no longer required to avoid memory leakage.

nodes.label: Growth Data Deserves Strong Protection
nodes.rationale: Unauthorized access to failures, habits, values and emotional states could enable psychological manipulation, so the companion core must actively resist third-party observation and OS-level scraping.

nodes.label: Memories Are Highly Sensitive
nodes.rationale: The cognitive database stores thoughts, reflections, workspace actions and emerging identity characteristics — the user's private mental space — so all stored memories carry the highest sensitivity classification.

nodes.label: Zero Third-Party Trust
nodes.rationale: Aggregation, memory recall and identity synthesis all occur locally; no raw telemetry or personal identifiers leave the device, and only anonymized filtered context packages may cross a network boundary.

nodes.label: tests/database-path-safety.test.ts
nodes.rationale: Ten regression tests across isolation, explicit override and production preservation, so the fix cannot silently regress the way the old per-file pattern did.

nodes.label: check_real_db.ts Resolver Bypass
nodes.rationale: Opens the production database directly, bypassing the resolver — but with zero importers and no npm script it is not part of the command surface, so it was recorded rather than changed.

nodes.label: RC-5 — Stale Local Test-Helper Calls and Dead Config
nodes.norm_label: rc-5 — stale local test-helper calls and dead config
nodes.rationale: 19 assertEquals/assertExists calls drifted from a convention 100 other call sites in the same file already followed.

nodes.label: ESM Import Hoisting Root Cause
nodes.rationale: In ESM every import declaration is hoisted and its module graph fully evaluated before any statement in the importing module's body runs, so a test assigning AKIRA_DATABASE_PATH on line 1 runs after module-scope singletons have already cached a production handle. The per-file protection pattern is structurally incapable of working.

nodes.label: In-Memory Database Default Under Test
nodes.rationale: Chosen over a temp file because it cannot leak to disk, needs no cleanup, and makes the safe default unconditional rather than dependent on each test remembering to opt in. Environment signals were verified rather than assumed, and explicit overrides plus production runtime behaviour are unchanged.

nodes.label: D0 — The Entire Vault Test Suite Was Dead
nodes.norm_label: d0 — the entire vault test suite was dead
nodes.rationale: Four Vault test files declared cases through a local test() helper vitest never saw, and two wrapped each case in try/catch that only console.error-ed failures — reporting success regardless. Vault regression protection at baseline was zero, and the existing reference-counting case walked straight through the D2 scenario without checking the survivor.

nodes.label: D1 — Path Traversal via Prefix Matching
nodes.norm_label: d1 — path traversal via prefix matching
nodes.rationale: resolved.startsWith(root) does not respect path segment boundaries, so any sibling directory whose name merely begins with the Vault root's name escaped the sandbox. The one traversal case the tests covered escaped past the shared prefix and was blocked, hiding the single-level sibling hole.

nodes.label: D2 — Soft Delete Destroys a Deduplicated Sibling's Content
nodes.norm_label: d2 — soft delete destroys a deduplicated sibling's content
nodes.rationale: Physical file lifetime was decided per record while storage is shared per path, so renaming the file into Trash and updating only the deleted record left every other deduplicated record dangling.

nodes.label: D3 — Dedup Against Soft-Deleted Records and Hash-Based Cleanup
nodes.norm_label: d3 — dedup against soft-deleted records and hash-based cleanup
nodes.rationale: getByHash returned soft-deleted rows, so a new upload could be registered live while pointing at bytes sitting in the bin; and permanentDeleteFile counted references by content hash, which is not the ownership key, both orphaning files forever and appearing to protect bytes it did not describe.

nodes.label: Storage Path as the Ownership Key
nodes.norm_label: storage path as the ownership key
nodes.rationale: The unifying cause of D2 and D3: the code had no single answer to 'who owns these bytes?'. Deduplication created shared ownership while delete, restore and purge each reasoned by a different key (record identity, then content hash) and never by the storage path that actually identifies the bytes.

nodes.label: Every Persistent Read or Write Flows Through a Repository
nodes.norm_label: every persistent read or write flows through a repository
nodes.rationale: Direct SQL, direct SQLite client imports and storage access outside the persistence layer are prohibited, so data access has exactly one auditable seam.

nodes.label: Platform-Appropriate Protection
nodes.rationale: Implementations must leverage the OS's secure credential storage and native file-access controls so other local applications or scripts cannot read the user databases.

nodes.label: Preservation of Privacy and Ownership
nodes.rationale: The user owns their data: the security model must preserve absolute privacy without restricting backup, export, migration or deletion, and encryption keys and data paths stay under the user's control.
